subject: orientation
question: What is the correct learning path in Pawan Satoshi Academy, from start to finish?
options: Orientation → Class 1 → Class 2 → ... → Class 12 → Graduation
Class 1 → Orientation → Graduation → Class 12
You can start at any class and finish in any order
Graduation → Orientation → Class 1
explanation: The Academy follows one fixed sequence: Orientation first, then Class 1 through Class 12 in order, then Graduation. Each class builds on the one before it.

subject: orientation
question: How much does it cost to join, learn, take quizzes, and earn certificates in the Academy?
options: Free for everything, forever
Free to join, but certificates cost money
A one-time fee to unlock all classes
Free for beginners, paid for advanced classes
explanation: Free Forever is a core principle of the Academy. Joining, learning, quizzes, and certificates never require payment — this is a permanent policy, not a promotional offer.

subject: orientation
question: Where do you go to find lessons for every subject, from Orientation through Graduation?
options: The Academy Hub forum channel
A different text channel for each of the 22 subjects
Only the website — Discord has no lesson content at all
The #general-chat channel
explanation: All curriculum content lives as organized threads inside one Academy Hub forum channel, rather than being spread across dozens of separate channels. This keeps navigation simple even though the curriculum is large.

subject: orientation
question: What do you need to do before the rest of the server unlocks for you?
options: Read the rules and complete verification in #verify
Wait 24 hours after joining
Message a moderator directly and ask for access
Post an introduction in #general-chat
explanation: New members only see the START HERE category until they read the rules and click the verification button in #verify. That action assigns the Verified role, which unlocks the full server.

subject: orientation
question: Which of these best reflects the Academy's community philosophy?
options: Learn before earn, and verify information before trusting it
Earn first, learning is optional
Trust every link and message from other members
Compete with other members rather than help them
explanation: The community values state: learn before earn, verify before trusting, respect everyone, and help beginners. Especially in a Web3-adjacent community, verifying information before trusting it protects you from scams.

subject: orientation
question: A staff member DMs you asking for your wallet seed phrase to 'verify your account.' What should you do?
options: Never share it — no legitimate staff member will ever ask for this
Share it, since they said they're staff
Share only the first few words of the phrase
Ask them to prove they're staff first, then share it
explanation: Nobody legitimate — not staff, not mentors, not the Owner — will ever ask for your seed phrase or private keys. This is always a scam, regardless of who appears to be asking.

subject: orientation
question: How do you progress from the 'Verified' role to the 'Active' role?
options: By earning XP through participation, quizzes, and challenges
By paying a membership fee
Automatically after 1 day in the server
By asking an Admin to manually promote you
explanation: Role progression (Verified → Active → OG) is XP-based, earned through genuine participation like quizzes and daily challenges — not manual staff promotion or payment.

subject: orientation
question: You're stuck on a lesson and have a specific question. Where should you ask it?
options: #questions or #help
DM the server Owner directly
Post it in #announcements
Wait until the next Sunday meeting
explanation: #questions and #help are the dedicated channels for getting unstuck. Mentors and other members actively watch these channels — you don't need to wait for a scheduled event or contact the Owner directly for routine questions.

subject: orientation
question: What is the role of a Mentor in the Academy?
options: To help members learn — answering questions and holding office hours
To have the same authority as the server Owner
To decide who gets banned
To manage the GitHub repository
explanation: Mentors focus specifically on helping members learn: answering questions, encouraging progress, and holding office hours. They don't have Owner-level authority or repository management responsibilities by default.

subject: orientation
question: When does the Academy's regular community meeting happen?
options: Sunday at 7 PM IST
Every day at midnight
Only once a month
There is no regular meeting
explanation: The weekly community meeting — Q&A, quiz, announcements, roadmap updates — happens every Sunday at 7 PM IST in the #weekly-meeting voice channel.

subject: orientation
question: What do you need to do to earn a certificate at each level?
options: Complete the required lessons and pass the required quizzes
Pay a certificate issuance fee
Simply join the server
Be nominated by another member
explanation: Certificates are earned, not purchased or granted socially — you complete the required lessons and pass the quiz/exam threshold for that level (Orientation, Foundation, Intermediate, Advanced, Graduation).

subject: orientation
question: Which of these is NOT one of the Academy's quiz types?
options: Pay-to-skip Exam
Daily Quiz
Weekly Quiz
Monthly Exam
explanation: There is no way to pay to skip an exam — that would violate the Academy's free-forever, no-shortcuts policy. The real quiz types are Daily, Weekly, Monthly Exam, and Practice Mode.

subject: orientation
question: Is Pawan Satoshi Academy only about cryptocurrency and Web3?
options: No — it also covers digital literacy, cyber security, AI, and programming basics
Yes, it's exclusively focused on crypto trading
Yes, but only for advanced blockchain developers
No, it excludes Web3 entirely
explanation: The curriculum was deliberately expanded beyond crypto to serve absolute beginners: Internet Basics, Digital Literacy, Cyber Security, AI, Git/GitHub, Linux, and Programming are taught alongside Bitcoin, Blockchain, Ethereum, and other Web3 topics.

subject: orientation
question: You spot a scam link posted in a channel. What's the best first action?
options: Report it to a moderator/admin rather than clicking it or replying to it
Click the link to see if it's really a scam
Reply to the message warning others, then ignore it
DM the person who posted it asking why
explanation: Reporting suspicious content to staff is safer and more effective than investigating it yourself. The Academy also runs automated scam/phishing detection, but a human report is still the fastest way to get something reviewed.

subject: orientation
question: What is the purpose of Practice Mode quizzes?
options: Low-pressure practice on a subject of your choice, anytime
The only way to earn a certificate
A once-a-year mandatory exam
A leaderboard-only competitive mode
explanation: Practice Mode lets you quiz yourself on any subject, anytime, without it counting toward a formal exam or deadline — it's there purely to help you learn and self-check understanding.

subject: orientation
question: What does clicking 'I Accept the Rules' in #verify actually do, technically?
options: It assigns you the Verified role, which unlocks other channels via permission settings
It sends your personal data to the Academy
It automatically enrolls you in Class 1
It changes your Discord username
explanation: Behind the scenes, the button click triggers the bot to assign the Verified Discord role to your account. Every other category's visibility is controlled by permission overwrites tied to that role — that's the whole mechanism.

subject: orientation
question: What's the difference between the Leaderboard and the Hall of Fame?
options: Leaderboard shows current XP rankings; Hall of Fame recognizes standout achievements over time
They are the exact same thing with two different names
Leaderboard is for staff only; Hall of Fame is for everyone
Hall of Fame requires a paid subscription
explanation: The Leaderboard is a live, ongoing ranking based on XP. Hall of Fame is a more curated space recognizing notable achievements and contributions, updated periodically rather than in real time.

subject: orientation
question: The Academy describes itself as 'open-source first.' What does that mean in practice?
options: The bot and website code are maintained in a public GitHub repository anyone can inspect or contribute to
Only staff can ever see the source code
The curriculum content is kept secret until graduation
It means the Discord server itself is open to the public internet outside Discord
explanation: Open-source first means the actual bot code, automation, and much of the documentation live in a public GitHub repository — anyone can read it, learn from it, and contribute improvements via pull requests.

subject: orientation
question: In the Academy's role hierarchy, who has the final override authority over every automated action?
options: The Owner
Any Moderator
The bot itself, with no human override
Whoever has been a member the longest
explanation: The Owner always retains full override control — no automation, bot, or staff role can act in a way the Owner cannot review, reverse, or disable. This is a deliberate, non-negotiable safety principle of the whole system.

subject: orientation
question: Why does the Academy use one Academy Hub forum channel instead of a separate text channel for each of the 22 subjects?
options: To keep the server simple and beginner-friendly by avoiding channel overload, while still covering the full curriculum
Because Discord doesn't allow more than 10 channels per server
Because forum channels are cheaper to run
Because subjects are taught in a random, unstructured order
explanation: A separate channel per subject would mean dozens of channels, which overwhelms new members. Forum threads let the full 22-subject curriculum exist without that channel sprawl — content is organized by topic within one forum instead.

subject: orientation
question: Where should you go for long-form lessons, documentation, and downloadable study material?
options: The GitHub Pages website
Discord voice channels
The #announcements channel
Direct messages from staff
explanation: Discord is optimized for discussion, quizzes, and events — long-form reading material lives on the GitHub Pages website instead, since that's a better format for extended reading, especially on mobile.

subject: orientation
question: If you type something like 'I am new' in a chat channel, what is the AI helper designed to do?
options: Recognize the intent and guide you step by step starting from Orientation
Ignore it completely — the AI only responds to slash commands
Immediately assign you a certificate
Kick you from the server for testing the bot
explanation: The AI helper is designed to recognize onboarding intent in natural language and proactively walk a new member through Orientation, rather than requiring them to already know which command or channel to use.

subject: orientation
question: Why does the Academy keep its original third-party bots (like Welcomer or MEE6) running even while building a custom bot?
options: So the community is never left without welcome/moderation/XP functionality during the transition
Because the custom bot is not allowed to have those features
Because third-party bots are mandatory forever
It doesn't — all old bots were removed immediately
explanation: The migration follows a build → test → explicit approval → retire sequence. Old bots stay active until their custom replacement is proven to work, so the community never experiences a gap in functionality.

subject: orientation
question: The Academy is designed to be usable entirely from which kind of device?
options: A mobile phone — no desktop required
Only a desktop computer with special software installed
A gaming console
It requires specialized hardware
explanation: Mobile-first is a core design principle — every workflow, from learning to quizzes to server administration, is built to work from a phone browser or the Discord/GitHub mobile apps.

subject: orientation
question: What is 'progressive unlock' as used in the Academy's server design?
options: New members see only a small set of channels at first; more unlocks as they verify and progress
Every channel is visible to everyone from the moment they join
Channels unlock based on how much money a member has spent
It refers to unlocking Discord Nitro features
explanation: Progressive unlock means the server doesn't show its full complexity at once. A brand-new member sees a small START HERE set; verifying unlocks the rest — this prevents the classic 'wall of channels' overwhelm.

subject: orientation
question: What is the #tickets channel for?
options: Opening a private support request that only you and staff can see
Buying event tickets for real-world meetups
Posting public complaints about other members
Submitting quiz answers
explanation: The ticket system creates a private space for a member and staff to resolve something one-on-one, rather than airing account or personal issues in a public channel.

subject: orientation
question: You have an idea to improve the Academy. Where should you post it?
options: #suggestions
#scam-alerts
#hall-of-fame
Nowhere — members can't influence Academy decisions
explanation: #suggestions exists specifically so members can propose improvements. The Academy explicitly describes itself as community-driven — member feedback is expected, not just tolerated.

subject: orientation
question: What would you post in #showcase?
options: A project or achievement you're proud of, like a completed assignment or personal build
A complaint about another member
A scam link you found
Your private wallet address for donations
explanation: #showcase is for celebrating what members have built or accomplished — it's a positive, achievement-focused space, distinct from general chat or support channels.

subject: orientation
question: When a channel is no longer actively used, what does the Academy do with it?
options: Moves it into the Archive category instead of deleting it
Deletes it immediately to save space
Leaves it exactly where it was, cluttering the active categories
Bans everyone who posted in it
explanation: The Academy's policy is to archive old content rather than delete it — this preserves history and past discussions while keeping the active parts of the server uncluttered.

subject: orientation
question: What is the #study-groups forum for?
options: Finding or forming a small group of members learning the same material together
Reporting bugs in the bot
Posting your final exam answers publicly
Requesting a refund
explanation: Study groups let members pair up or form small groups to work through lessons together — peer learning is part of how the Academy supports members outside scheduled events.

subject: orientation
question: At what point in the curriculum does Career Guidance content appear?
options: At Graduation, alongside the capstone project and final exam
In Orientation only
It's not part of the curriculum at all
Randomly inserted between every class
explanation: Career Guidance is part of the Graduation stage — by then, a member has the foundational and technical knowledge needed to make sense of career-oriented advice.

subject: orientation
question: Besides learning, what else does the Academy's #gaming channel and voice channels support?
options: Free community activities like chess, to build community outside of coursework
Paid tournament entry
Gambling
Nothing — the Academy has no non-learning content
explanation: The Academy intentionally includes free entertainment like chess and games, using Discord's built-in Activities where supported — never anything requiring payment or Nitro.

subject: orientation
question: What is the Academy's approach to collecting member data?
options: Collect only the minimum needed to operate the community, and never sell it
Collect as much personal data as possible for analytics
Sell member data to advertisers to keep the Academy free
Require a government ID to join
explanation: The privacy principle is minimal collection: only what's needed to run the community (like XP or quiz progress), and member data is never sold — this is explicit Academy policy, not just a default.

subject: orientation
question: If you receive a warning or ban you believe was a mistake, what can you do?
options: Use the documented appeal process, reviewed by staff
Nothing — all moderation decisions are final and unappealable
Create a second account to bypass it
Post publicly attacking the moderator who issued it
explanation: Warnings and bans have a documented, staff-reviewed appeal process. Members are not left with no recourse if they believe a moderation action was wrong.

subject: orientation
question: Can you advertise your own project or channel in the Academy?
options: Only in designated self-promotion channels, and never as unsolicited spam elsewhere
Yes, anywhere and anytime you want
No, self-promotion is completely banned everywhere
Only if you pay a promotion fee to the Academy
explanation: Self-promotion is allowed, but confined to designated spaces — it isn't free-for-all advertising in every channel, and unsolicited promotion outside those spaces is treated as spam.

subject: orientation
question: Why does the Academy refuse to give the Administrator permission to any bot, including its own custom bot?
options: Least-privilege security: a bot only gets exactly the permissions its features need, limiting damage if something goes wrong
Discord technically doesn't allow bots to have Administrator
Administrator permission costs extra on Discord
It's an arbitrary rule with no security reasoning
explanation: This is a deliberate least-privilege security principle: if a bot is ever compromised or bugged, its damage potential is limited to only the specific permissions it was granted — not full server control.

subject: orientation
question: How does the Academy protect the server from explicit/NSFW image content, without paying for a third-party image-scanning service?
options: By using Discord's own built-in Explicit Content Filter, set to scan media from all members
By manually reviewing every image a member posts
By banning all image uploads entirely
It doesn't protect against this at all
explanation: Discord provides a free, native Explicit Content Filter that can scan uploaded images. Setting it to the strictest level (scanning all members) satisfies NSFW protection without any paid API.

subject: orientation
question: If a large number of suspicious new accounts join the server in a short burst, what is likely to happen automatically?
options: The server temporarily raises its verification requirements and may remove very new accounts as a precaution
Nothing — the Academy has no automated protection against this
The entire server is deleted
All existing members are kicked
explanation: The Academy's anti-raid system detects unusually fast join bursts and responds automatically: temporarily raising verification level and removing very new accounts, then reverting once things are calm again.

subject: orientation
question: How does the Academy keep a record of important actions like role changes or moderation decisions?
options: Through an audit log system that staff can review with a command
There is no record kept of anything
Only the Owner's personal memory
Screenshots posted manually by members
explanation: The Academy's audit system logs bot-driven actions and mirrors Discord's own native audit log into a staff-reviewable trail, so nothing important happens without a traceable record.

subject: orientation
question: If a mentor or member tells you a crypto investment is 'guaranteed' to make you money, what should you think?
options: Be skeptical — Academy mentors are guided not to guarantee investment returns, and no legitimate source can promise that
Trust it completely since it came from inside the community
Invest everything you have immediately
Assume it must be true because they're a Mentor
explanation: Mentor guidelines explicitly state mentors should never guarantee profits or investment returns. Any 'guaranteed returns' claim, from anyone, is a red flag worth treating with suspicion.

subject: orientation
question: Community Management is one of the 22 curriculum subjects. What does it broadly prepare you for?
options: Skills for helping run and grow an online community, like moderation basics and engagement
Only how to use Microsoft Excel
Physical event catering
Stock market day-trading
explanation: Community Management, taught later in the curriculum, covers the practical skills behind running healthy online communities — directly useful given the Academy is itself a community members can help grow.

subject: orientation
question: Why does the Academy's quiz bank vary in size per subject (some subjects have far more questions than others) instead of a fixed number for every subject?
options: Because question count should match how much genuine, non-repetitive content a topic actually supports — quality over an arbitrary quota
Because writing more questions is technically impossible for some subjects
Because larger subjects are more important and deserve more attention regardless of quality
The bank size is actually always identical for every subject
explanation: A mastery-based approach avoids padding small topics with repetitive filler just to hit a quota, and avoids under-covering large topics just to keep things even. The right size is however many genuinely distinct, high-quality questions a topic supports.
